skill.name: threejs-interaction
skill.description: Add camera navigation, object picking, dragging, and selection to Three.js scenes. The examples target Three.js r186 and cover WebGL and WebGPU.
skill.summary: Build Three.js camera controls, object picking, and transform interactions.
skill.author: cloudai-x

content.value_statement: Object picking and camera controls can conflict when they share the same canvas. Use Three.js examples to map pointer input, select objects, and coordinate camera movement with editing tools.
actual_capabilities: Convert pointer positions into canvas-relative rays and filter intersections by object list, layer, or distance.
Configure orbit, map, fly, first-person, pointer-lock, or trackball camera controls.
Add move, rotate, and scale gizmos with snapping, and pause orbiting during gizmo drags.
Drag meshes directly with DragControls or constrain movement to a plane using raycasting.
Add click selection, hover feedback, and rectangle selection with Three.js helpers.
Adapt camera controls to WebGPU and use proxy geometry for meshes displaced on the GPU.
limitations: The examples target Three.js r186. Other releases may need API changes.
The skill provides JavaScript examples, not a packaged scene editor or a complete application.
CPU raycasting cannot detect displacement applied by GPU shaders. An undisplaced proxy only approximates the rendered surface.
Box selection tests object centers rather than selecting every mesh that overlaps the rectangle.

use_cases.title: Make a product viewer interactive
use_cases.description: Let visitors orbit a product and highlight the nearest selectable part when they click or tap.

use_cases.title: Add first-person navigation
use_cases.description: Use pointer lock and frame-time updates to move a first-person camera through a browser scene.

use_cases.title: Build a scene editing tool
use_cases.description: Add rectangle selection and a transform gizmo with snapping. Pause orbiting while users drag the gizmo.

prompt_templates.title: Pick a Mesh
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: An existing scene needs click or tap selection.
prompt_templates.prompt: Add pointer selection to my Three.js r186 canvas. Use canvas-relative coordinates and highlight the nearest selectable mesh.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Orbit Navigation
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: A product viewer needs predictable camera movement.
prompt_templates.prompt: Add OrbitControls to my product viewer with damping and zoom limits. Show the frame update and explain how to dispose of the controls.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate the Transform Gizmo and Camera
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: An editor needs object manipulation without camera movement during drags.
prompt_templates.prompt: Attach a transform gizmo to the selected mesh and configure snapping for translation, rotation, and scale. Pause orbiting during gizmo drags and restore it when the drag ends.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt Picking to WebGPU
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: A WebGPU scene displaces meshes in a shader.
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt my Three.js picking and orbit controls to WebGPURenderer. Use proxy geometry on a dedicated picking layer. Explain where the proxy may differ from the visible mesh.

output_examples.input: Clicks select the wrong mesh when the canvas is below a toolbar.
output_examples.output: Use the canvas bounds to normalize the pointer position. Raycast only against selectable meshes, then highlight the nearest hit or clear the selection when nothing is hit.

output_examples.input: The camera rotates when I drag the scale gizmo.
output_examples.output: Disable orbit input when the gizmo starts dragging and restore it when the drag ends. Add the gizmo helper, not the controls object, to the scene.

output_examples.input: My selection rectangle does not select a mesh that touches its edge.
output_examples.output: SelectionBox checks the center of the mesh's bounding sphere. An overlapping edge does not qualify when the center is outside the selection volume.

best_practices: Measure pointer coordinates against the canvas bounds and raycast only against objects users can select.
Update time-dependent controls each frame with elapsed seconds from Three.js Timer.
Keep references to event handlers so you can remove them, and dispose of controls and timers during teardown.
anti_patterns: Normalize pointer coordinates against the full window when the canvas is embedded or offset.
Let OrbitControls and the transform gizmo respond to the same drag.
Assume CPU raycasting detects a surface displaced by a shader.

faq.question: Which Three.js release do the examples target?
faq.answer: They target Three.js r186. Check your installed release before reusing the imports and control methods.

faq.question: Do camera controls work with both WebGL and WebGPU?
faq.answer: Yes. The controls and Raycaster are independent of the renderer, but WebGPURenderer has a separate initialization step.

faq.question: Can I use the same picking handler for mouse and touch?
faq.answer: Yes. DOM pointer events can handle mouse, touch, and pen input with the same listener.

faq.question: Can I pick invisible objects?
faq.answer: Yes. Raycaster tests layers rather than visibility, so an invisible proxy can represent a complex object.

faq.question: When should I use DragControls instead of TransformControls?
faq.answer: Use DragControls for direct dragging. Use TransformControls when users need visible handles, axis-based edits, or snapping.

faq.question: Does pointer lock require a user gesture?
faq.answer: Yes. Request pointer lock after a deliberate user action such as clicking an entry button.
